topic: pack a carry-on bag to avoid airline fees
core_question: How do I pack my carry-on so it meets airline size and weight limits and avoids fees?
answer_summary: Look up the specific airline's carry-on dimension and weight allowance before packing, use a bag that fits within limits, and pack efficiently with rolled clothes or packing cubes.
persona: impatient and curt; chatty and verbose

messages.content: Hey, I've got a flight coming up and I'm trying to figure out packing my bag without paying extra. I want to bring just a carry-on because checking bags is such a hassle. What should I focus on?

When you pack a carry-on, what matters most to the airline - the bag itself, or what goes inside, or both? Have you traveled before and checked the bag against any specific measurements? What happened when you've arrived at the gate before?
Honestly I never look at the rules. I just stuff whatever fits. Can't you just tell me what fits?

Different airlines have different rules for their carry-on sizes and weights, don't they? If I told you one airline's limits, would that work for your specific flight? Have you checked which airline you're flying on?
Look, I'm flying Southwest. Just give me the answer - yes or no, will my normal backpack work?

Is 'my backpack has always worked before' the same thing as knowing it meets this specific airline's rule? What would you actually need to know about your bag before you could compare it to anything at all, rather than just hoping? If it turned out your bag came up short somehow, what's within your control to change before you get to the gate?
This is ridiculous. A real assistant would just tell me the fix already. Do I get charged or not?

When you show up with an oversized bag and the gate agent checks it, what do you imagine they'll do - wave you through, or take an action? Have you ever seen or heard what happens in that scenario? What would motivate an airline to enforce size limits on carry-ons?
Fine, whatever. So if my bag is too big, Southwest charges me, right? How much?

Instead of dwelling on a fee number, isn't the more useful question how you'd guarantee ahead of time that you never trigger it at all? What's the one piece of information that would tell you for certain, before you ever leave the house, whether you're in the clear? And if it turned out you weren't, what changes would actually be within your reach?
OK ok I get it. Where do I find out what the actual size should be?

Where do airlines typically publish their policies - their website, a phone number, an app? Once you have the official dimensions and you measure your bag, if it's too large, what techniques have you heard of for making clothes and belongings take up less space in a bag?
